source: Hi. Make An FPS Shooter Game With A Loading GUI. Once Loaded On The Main Hub Screen, Have A Button Where It Says Play An When Clicking It. it Loads You Onto The Map\n\nMake The Map First. the Map Style Will Be Like The Hood But A Bit Different.

image_prompt.text: Waist-high and full-body cover distributed evenly along every street and alley
Narrow alley pinches where the streets meet, concentrating fights into contested ground
Two team bases at opposite ends of the neighbourhood, screened from enemy sightlines by buildings

layout_placement.text: Balanced team spawns at opposite ends of the neighbourhood, shielded from enemy sniper lines

notes: Team Deathmatch preset taken whole; the prompt never named a mode, so team play and cover arrays are preset-derived.
The hub screen, loading GUI, and play button are not layout and are carried as unmatched requests.

open_questions.ask: What mode is this - team deathmatch, free-for-all, or an objective?
What should be different about your hood map compared to the one you have in mind?
How many blocks should the neighbourhood cover?

coverage_missing.ask: What mode is this - team deathmatch, free-for-all, or an objective?
What should be different about your hood map compared to the reference?
How many blocks should the neighbourhood cover?

answers.ask: What mode is this - team deathmatch, free-for-all, or an objective?
answers.answer: Make it free-for-all so players spawn into the map and fight each other.

answers.ask: What should be different about your hood map compared to the one you have in mind?
answers.answer: Keep a hood/neighbourhood feel, but make it an original layout with different streets, buildings, and landmarks rather than copying a specific map.

answers.ask: How many blocks should the neighbourhood cover?
answers.answer: Use a small map covering about 4 city blocks so it is easy to play and build.
